questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's MCP guide recommend when choosing a remote MCP server?

options.text: Pick the server with the most tools, so one server covers many needs.
options.explanation: The guide's advice is about who runs the server, not how many tools it has.

options.text: Pick an official server hosted by the service provider itself.
options.explanation: Right. Its example is Stripe's server hosted by Stripe, not a third-party copy.

options.text: Pick any server, because OpenAI verifies them all first.
options.explanation: The guide says remote MCP servers have not been verified by OpenAI.

questions.prompt: What does the modelcontextprotocol/servers README say about its reference servers?

options.text: They are educational examples, not production-ready solutions.
options.explanation: Right. Developers should check their own security needs and add safeguards.

options.text: They are security-audited and safe for any company data.
options.explanation: The README says the opposite: they are examples, not production-ready.

options.text: They replace the official servers of each service.
options.explanation: The README calls them reference implementations to show MCP features.

questions.prompt: In OpenAI's MCP guide, what is the status of built-in connectors (connector_id)?

options.text: They are the recommended way to connect every new model.
options.explanation: The guide points new work to remote MCP servers instead.

options.text: They were removed from every model, old and new.
options.explanation: The guide says existing models keep connector support.

options.text: Legacy: deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026.
options.explanation: Right. The guide says to use a remote MCP server (server_url) or Secure MCP Tunnel instead.
